1| # driftwatch spool
2| 
3| The spool is the durable buffer between ingest and the exporter. Every
4| accepted batch lands in the spool before the ingest response is sent,
5| so an accepted write survives a crash or an exporter outage.
6| 
7| ## Layout
8| 
9| Spool data lives under the data directory as numbered segment files.
10| Segments are append-only; a segment that has rolled is immutable and
11| is eligible for retention sweeps once exported.
12| 
13| ## Pacing
14| 
15| Buffered batches drain to the active segment on a fixed cadence. The
16| shipped default flushes twice a minute; deployments tune this per
17| profile through the config layer. Lowering the cadence smooths disk
18| pressure at the cost of a slightly larger replay window after a crash.
19| 
20| ## Sizing
21| 
22| Keep the spool on local disk, not network storage. Size it for at
23| least a day of peak ingest so an exporter outage over a weekend does
24| not force retention sweeps to run early.
